summary_md: **恒星sun ([@vintcessun](https://x.com/vintcessun/status/2115676009123189144))** (in Chinese) summarizes a paper that treats agents as having OS-level power without OS-level protection: across 19 subsystems and 116 mechanisms only 11 match traditional OS designs and 65 are missing (privilege separation, quotas, tamper-proof audit), and experiments on three CLIs found single-tool guards bypassable via shell and forged session records accepted on resume.

referenced_urls.title: Ring-0 by Default: Agents as Operating Systems (AaOS)

relevance: Maps missing OS-style protections in coding-agent CLIs, with concrete bypasses.

media.description: Table 2 from the Agent-as-OS paper: a reference-monitor audit showing defenses expressed as model input (system-prompt rules, spotlighting, instruction hierarchy, StruQ/SecAlign) fail tamper-proofness, while external ones (hooks, IFC/dual-LLM, capability gating, runtime constraint DSL, monitoring, formal policy enforcement, host sandbox) can be relied on.

Columns: Non-byp. / Tamper-pf. / Verif.

media.description: Timeline mapping OS responsibilities (action loop, tool interface, drivers/MCP, memory, file I/O, packaging/skills, autostart, suspend/resume, multi-agent IPC) to their first release in widely used agents (ReAct, AutoGPT, function calling, MCP, MemGPT, SWE-agent, Agent Skills, A2A) and the missing protection in each (e.g. no signing, no ACL, sender label is text).

Stacked bar chart classifying agent-OS counterparts across 19 OS subsystems (process, scheduling, memory, filesystem, IPC, network, identity, isolation, accounting, state, etc.): 65 missing (56%), 26 degraded (22%), 14 mutated (12%), 11 isomorphic (9%), plus 9 novel.
media.ocr_text: Missing 65 (56%) no counterpart · Degraded 26 (22%) present, weaker · Mutated 14 (12%) other meaning · Isomorphic 11 (9%) same protection · Novel 9 no OS analogue
